page.layout: Two coin medallions side by side at the top, with woodcut portraits and legends (illustrations, not text). Below them one column of running text. A decorative woodcut ornament at the foot of the page. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: CONSTANTINVS, natu maximus filiorum Con-stantini Magni,patre mortuo,anno mundi 4301.à Christo na-to 338.imperat vnà cum fratribus Constante & Constantio. hi, siue ex testamento patris,siue ex propria eorum voluntate, Imperium ita partiti sunt, vt Constantinus Gallias, Hispanias,Britanniamque insulam obtineret: Constans Italiam cum Illyrico & Græciam:Constantius Byzantiū cum Oriente,qui Dalmatium patruelē Imperij socium haberet, quē postea militari factione oppressit. Nec durat diu fratrum cōcordia:nam Constantinus Gallico exercitu fretus, Constãti bellum infert:quod dum cupidius quàm cautius gerit,exceptus insidiis,vulneribúsq; con-fossus perit,ad Aquileiam,anno ætatis suæ 25.Imperij 3.Consu-lito Pomp.Læt.& Bap. Egna.li.1.

LICINIVS,iunior,Constantini Magni ex sorore Con-stantia nepos,creatus est Cæsar vnà cum Crispo,eiusdem Con-stantini ex Mineruina concubina filio,anno mundi 4278.à Christo nato 316. verùm hi factione infaustæ Faustæ interfi-ciuntur.Aur. Vict. Pomponius Læt.hic Crispus à Lactantio fuit eruditus.

page.notes: Coin legends are part of the woodcut illustrations and are not transcribed as text: left coin "CONSTANTINVS.AVG."; right coin "IMP.LICINIVS P.F AVG" and "D.N.CRISPVS NOB.". Bottom ornament is a decorative woodcut with no text. Spacing around some punctuation (e.g. "infert:quod", "Imperij 3.Consu-") is as printed, not normalised. "Vict." is printed with a ligature.
